subject: Amplidata private offer — procurement contacts, term options & buyer approval cadence
messages:
From: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@amplidata.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Private offer — term options and procurement path

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency and cost profile. Procurement wants to understand two things before we proceed: 1) whether Redwood can issue an AWS Marketplace private offer for both a 12-month and 24-month term and 2) a clear list of buyer approvals required on our side (finance, legal, procurement) so we can map the internal owner/ETA.

High level: we'll likely prefer the 24-month commit but need to confirm if there are additional approvals for multi-year private offers coming from AWS (e.g., finance signoff or legal redlines that typically add time). Can you also include a contact at AWS (seller support) if we need help expediting?

CCing Mike O'Neil (procurement) who will own the purchase timeline.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Suresh
Head of Platform Partnerships
Amplidata
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Private offer — term options and procurement path

Laura / Vanessa — forwarding Amplidata's ask. Priya wants guidance on 12m vs 24m private offer flows and who signs on the buyer side. Initial thoughts:

- Pricing: propose two SKUs in the private offer: 12-month at list -10% and 24-month at list -18% (we can tweak).
- Buyer approvals: typically procurement + finance for renewals > $100k; legal only if customer requests contract redlines or custom terms (we try to avoid). For > $250k we often see buyer legal + exec sign-off.
- AWS handling: AWS Seller Support can create the private offer and set the term length. For multi-year commitments they sometimes require an internal approval for billing tenor — if so, seller-support needs to flag the PO for expedited processing.

Attachments: pricing_sheet_q4_v2.xlsx (draft numbers) and mutual_action_plan_amplidata.pdf (MAM).

Questions for you: do we want to pre-authorize a standard legal exhibit to reduce legal cycles? And who from Revenue Ops should sign off on discount approval?

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer — term options and procurement path

Quick clarifications based on recent AWS marketplace runs:

- Internal buyer approval tiers: <= $100k: procurement sign-off only; $100k-$250k: procurement + finance; > $250k: procurement + finance + legal (sometimes exec approval).
- For 24-month private offers we recommend adding an optional early-termination fee schedule rather than a full custom contract — avoids legal review in many cases.
- AWS Seller Support: open case referencing our partner ID and the intended term. They'll confirm whether the marketplace team needs to route the offer through a special approvals queue for >12-month terms.

I'll open the Seller Support case and add the Amplidata contact. Also looping Revenue Ops (we should get an official discount approval before sending any private offer to AWS).

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partnerships
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@amplidata.com>
Cc: Mike O'Neil <mike.oneil@amplidata.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed private offer options and next steps (Amplidata)

Hi Priya / Mike,

Thanks — attached is a short mutual action plan and a pricing sheet with the two options: 12-month (10% off list) and 24-month (18% off list). See high‑level next steps below: 

1) You confirm procurement contact (Mike) and internal ETA for approvals.
2) We will request discount approval from Revenue Ops (I will do this today).
3) Once approved, Redwood will request AWS to create the private offer (we'll provide SKUs + term + price).
4) AWS will generate the marketplace private offer link; buyer accepts via marketplace and then issues PO or DocuSign as needed.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_amplidata.pdf, pricing_sheet_q4_v2.xlsx.

Can you confirm whether Amplidata prefers Redwood to route the PO to AWS (marketplace flow) or if you prefer a signed DocuSign and then we route to AWS? The timeline we want to aim for is: pricing approval today, private offer submitted Mon, buyer acceptance by Wed next week. Is that workable for you?

Best,
Ben
From: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@amplidata.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike O'Neil <mike.oneil@amplidata.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed private offer options and next steps (Amplidata)

Ben — thanks. Mike confirms procurement will lead internal approvals. We prefer the 24-month option (18% off) if you can get Finance sign-off on the discount and provide a marketplace private offer link that allows us to accept and then send a PO. Our legal team will only review if there are special billing terms — otherwise they'll waive redlines.

Estimated timeline: procurement + finance by next Wednesday (24th). Legal will only need 2–3 business days if invoked. If Redwood can submit the private offer and copy AWS contact on the case that will help speed things.

Mike O'Neil
Sr. Procurement Manager (on behalf of Amplidata)
